analysis: Integration pass over the CI watchdog update. Reviewed the patch to .github/workflows/darkbloom-watchdog.yml, the changelog entry, the docs/developer/build.md update and the scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py comment and assertion. None of these touch provider runtime, coordinator wire handling, attestation or App Attest authorization, encryption, key custody or the prefix cache (TB-002, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011, TB-012; T-041, T-053). No threat-model asset (A-001 to A-020) is affected. The workflow changes keep the same trust posture: top-level permissions are unchanged, and the token is used only in an Authorization header to GitHub over https. Listings move from jq argv (--arg/--argjson) to temp files and stdin under an mktemp directory. This fixes an E2BIG availability failure and adds no injection surface, since names still pass through clean() and jq --arg is still used for small scalars. The stranded predicate is the main semantic change. A job is now timed from its own creation, and only a Darkbloom job that got a runner within the wait holds the rescue back. Partially stranded runs are now cancelled and re-run, including runs with still-running Darkbloom jobs. This is a CI availability and cost tradeoff, documented in the docs and changelog with the DARKBLOOM_WATCHDOG_MINUTES mitigation. It remains bounded by the once-per-run rescue, and the docs say only routed CI runs are affected, not release or signing runs. The new test assertion only adds a guard, and its regex is a heuristic. Unverified: the integration replay omitted 12 units, and the full workflow body beyond the patch hunks and the unchanged release and signing workflows were not visible. The claim that the copy matches the upstream d6d257c2 template cannot be checked from the supplied evidence. This is a CI-correctness question rather than a demonstrated security issue, so there are no findings.
